2021_07_fy22_proposed_budget_complete_do.paragraph: Oakland Schools, the Oakland County intermediate school district, presented its FY22 Proposed Budget Complete Document for the May 18, 2021 board meeting, with a 3.16.21 revision stamp on every page. Total proposed funding is $359.6 million against $364.3 million of expenditures across all funds, with property tax revenue budgeted to rise 2.7%, or $5.5 million, to $207,634,700. The single largest line is the Special Education Fund's PA-18 base distribution to local districts, budgeted at $140,386,800. The General Education Fund plans an intentional operating deficit of $(2,220,400) to fund pandemic-response and collaborative programs, including up to $5 million for Literacy Essentials Oakland.
2021_07_fy22_proposed_budget_complete_do.page:
**Issuer and scope**
Oakland Schools (Oakland County ISD, Michigan) — one of 56 Michigan ISDs established in 1962, serving 28 constituent districts. FY22 Proposed Budget Complete Document, meeting date May 18, 2021, footer stamp 3.16.21. Covers all governmental and proprietary funds plus grant and state-funded projects; fiduciary (custodial) funds are not presented. Budgets take effect July 1, 2021.

**Enterprise-wide totals, FY 2021-22**

| Funding source | Amount | Use of resources | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| Property taxes | $207.6 million | Salary, wage and benefits | $76.4 million |
| Other local and investment revenue | $32.2 million | Purchased services, supplies, dues/fees | $20.3 million |
| State source revenue | $18.8 million | Electric and natural gas utilities | $.9 million |
| Other financing sources and indirect | $8.9 million | Capital outlay | $5.6 million |
| Expected new grant award funding | $78.6 million | Transfers to LEAs and other funds | $166.0 million |
| Estimated grant carryover | $13.5 million | Grant related expenditures | $92.1 million |
| **Total** | **$359.6 million** | Payment on existing debt / **Total** | $3.0 million / **$364.3 million** |

**Three major operating funds**

| Fund | Revenue | Expenditures | Surplus/(Deficit) | Ending fund balance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| General Education (100) | $21,286,500 | $23,506,900 | $(2,220,400) | $2,540,800 |
| Special Education (200) | $164,267,600 | $164,258,900 | $8,700 | $11,430,400 |
| Career Focused Education (600) | $43,755,500 | $45,200,400 | $(1,444,900) | $3,997,800 |

Property taxes by fund: GEF $12,337,500; SEF $156,909,100; CFEF $38,388,100 — each up 2.70%, totaling $207,634,700. Property taxes supply 58% of GEF revenue, 95% of SEF revenue and 88% of CFEF revenue.

**Key assumptions**
Taxable values in Oakland County are expected to rise more than 3.75%, but the budget assumes another Headlee rollback — the seventh year in a row. Tax revenues have risen 23% since the recession ended in 2014 yet remain $14.8 million below pre-recession levels. Michigan Tax Tribunal reserve set at .25% of tax revenues, roughly $519,000. No across-the-board salary increases; non-union step growth 1.63%, union .43%. MPSERS blended retirement rate 28.23%; UAAL stabilization rate rises from 14.51% to 15.05%. FICA 7.65% on wages to $142,800 for calendar 2021. Health care hard caps for plan years beginning after 1/1/22: family $19,844.61, individual plus one $15,217.08, single $7,276.34, assuming 3.3% medical CPI growth.

**Programs and staffing**
PA-18 base distribution $140,386,800 plus $3,933,200 for group home, extraordinary, startup and Section 24 payments. Up to $5 million for Literacy Essentials Oakland; about $2 million for learning-loss programs; $1,551,950 in cooperative software and service subsidies (Illuminate DnA $718,300 largest). Staffing moves from 653.96 to 654.96 FTE, the change being a new 1.0 FTE Transportation Manager split 73%/25%/2% across the three major funds. Four technical campuses serve about 2,700 students.

**Other funds, grants, capital**
Grants total $92,051,400 (Fund 105 $34,354,600; Fund 205 $55,749,000; Fund 605 $1,947,800). Medicaid Fund 273 revenue and expenditures both $11,133,300. Debt service: $975,000 principal plus $2,045,400 interest, $3,020,400 total. The 5-Year Capital Outlay Plan, first read March 16, 2021, shows FY21–FY26 needs of $34,351,500.
2021_07_fy22_proposed_budget_complete_do.verbose:
**Identification.** Oakland Schools — one of 56 Michigan intermediate school districts established in 1962, an autonomous tax-supported district serving 28 constituent local districts in Oakland County — issued the FY22 Proposed Budget Complete Document for the May 18, 2021 board meeting. Every page carries the footer "FY 22 Proposed Budget" and the date stamp 3.16.21. Mission: "Oakland Schools: Learning today. Transforming tomorrow." Budgets are adopted effective July 1, 2021 and cover all governmental fund types, proprietary fund types and a summary of grant and state-funded projects; fiduciary (custodial) funds are not presented.

**Enterprise-wide totals.** Proposed total funding of $359.6 million comprises property taxes $207.6 million, other local and investment revenue $32.2 million, state source revenue $18.8 million, other financing sources and indirect revenue $8.9 million, expected new grant award funding $78.6 million and estimated grant carryover funding $13.5 million. Proposed total expenditures of $364.3 million comprise salary, wage and benefits $76.4 million; purchased services, supplies, dues/fees $20.3 million; electric and natural gas utilities $.9 million; capital outlay $5.6 million; transfers to LEAs and other funds $166.0 million; grant related expenditures $92.1 million; and payment on existing debt $3.0 million. Both figures are net of eliminated Risk Related Activity Fund amounts.

**Property taxes.** Revenue is budgeted to increase 2.7%, or $5.5 million, to $207,634,700 — General Education Fund $12,337,500, Special Education Fund $156,909,100, Career Focused Education Fund $38,388,100, each +2.70%. Oakland County taxable values are expected to increase more than 3.75%, but the budget anticipates another Headlee rollback, which would be the seventh year in a row. Tax revenues have increased 23% since the end of the recession in 2014 and remain $14.8 million below pre-recession levels; the Great Recession's 24.5% cumulative loss in taxable value produced $430.2 million of cumulative district revenue erosion through fiscal year 2021. The tax base is 70% principal residence and 30% non-principal residence. Michigan Tax Tribunal judgments have returned $12.8 million in property taxes over the past ten years; the FY 2021-22 MTT reserve is .25% of tax revenues, about $519,000 in expense.

**General Education Fund (100).** Revenue $21,286,500 — property taxes $12.3 million (58% of total), other local $2.5 million, state source $5.8 million, other financing sources $.7 million; total local sources $14,785,800 and state sources $5,790,900 (Section 81 general aid $3,902,300; Section 147c UAAL rate stabilization $1,614,700; Section 147a $119,600; State Payment in Lieu of Taxes $145,000). Expenditures $23,506,900: General Administration $1,815,600, Finance and Operations $9,002,300, Instructional Services $10,228,700, Plant & Fixed Charges $2,460,300. The planned operating deficit of $(2,220,400) is described as an intentional spend-down to fund collaborative and supplemental instructional programs. Ending fund equity $2,540,800 — $74,800 non-spendable prepaids and $2,466,000 unassigned, or 10.5% of budgeted expenditures, down from 16.8%. Department 085 Instruction & Pedagogy rises to $3,662,800 on supplemental learning programs; COVID-19 response is budgeted at $1.3 million. Five-year forecast total revenues reach $24,084,400 by 2026-27 with unassigned balance of $3,405,800 (14.2%).

**Special Education Fund (200).** Revenue $164,267,600 — property taxes $156.9 million (95% of total), local sources $157,088,700, state sources $6,948,900 (Special Ed Sec 51A $3,207,200; State Payment in Lieu of Taxes $1,843,700; Section 147c $1,520,000; Sec 51.a.2 $115,500; Sec 51f $265,500; School for Deaf/Blind 54 $197,900), indirect revenue $230,000. Expenditures $164,258,900, producing an $8,700 surplus. Ending equity $11,430,400: $13,800 non-spendable, $997,000 restricted (5.0% of budgeted expenditures), $10,419,600 restricted for future center facility renovations. The PA-18 base distribution is $140,386,800, up $3.8 million or 2.8%, plus $3,933,200 for group home and medical student support, incarcerated youth, startup assistance, extraordinary contingency, assistive technology and Section 24 payments. The FY 2020 audited fund balance exceeded the 5% target, prompting a supplemental PA-18 distribution of $5.6 million in FY 2021 that does not recur. District distributions include Bloomfield Hills $10,707,800, Rochester $10,386,300, Walled Lake $10,174,300, Farmington $9,725,900, Birmingham $9,110,200, Waterford $8,564,500, Troy $7,330,500, Southfield $6,541,500, Hazel Park $6,372,100, Lake Orion $6,146,300, Clarkston $5,407,100, Huron Valley $5,502,900, Royal Oak $4,575,500, Pontiac $4,002,000, Public School Academies $1,558,800 and $2,000,000 "to be distributed." The Hazel Park center facility renovation project is complete, dropping that line to zero. Services support approximately 21,185 students with an IEP. Forecast LEA base distributions reach $163,758,000 by 2026-27.

**Career Focused Education Fund (600).** Revenue $43,755,500 — property taxes $38.4 million (88% of total), state sources $4,874,500 including Section 61a.1 at $1,422,000 (a 20% reduction reflecting pandemic effects on CTE completers), Section 147c $2,549,000, Section 147a $188,800 and State Payment in Lieu of Taxes $451,100. Expenditures $45,200,400: campus and other program operations $26,514,100, LEA transfers and program subsidies $5,843,000, plant and fixed charges $12,843,300; operating deficit $(1,444,900). Ending equity $3,997,800 — $25,200 non-spendable and $3,972,600 restricted, 8.8% of expenditures. Four Oakland Schools Technical Campuses serve approximately 2,700 students from all 28 districts: NW $5,552,300, SE $5,803,800, NE $6,095,900, SW $5,880,200. Nineteen state CTE program codes are submitted under Public Act 451 of 1976, MCL 380.684, as amended by Public Act 45 of 2007, including Cosmetology (NE only), Cyber Security and Public Safety (SE only), and Medium & Heavy Truck Technician (SW only). LEA transportation support is $1,800,000 annually and K-12 Career Readiness LEA support $3,088,000; STEM mobile classroom operating costs are $412,000 per year.

**Personnel and benefits.** Total staffing moves from 633.59 FTE in 2019-20 to 653.96 in 2020-21 to 654.96 in 2021-22, a change of 1.00 — a new 1.0 FTE Transportation Manager split 73% GEF, 25% SEF, 2% CFEF, previously a part-time retiree position. No across-the-board pay increases; non-union salary/wage step growth 1.63%, union wage growth .43%. The state-mandated retirement structure has eight rates; the most common, Basic/MIP with Health Care Premium Subsidy, is 28.21% through September 30, 2021 and a projected 28.23% from October 1, 2021, the blended budgeting rate. The MPSERS UAAL stabilization rate rises from 14.51% to 15.05%. FICA is 7.65%, with Social Security at 6.2% on wages to $142,800 for calendar year 2021. Health care "hard cap" limits for plan years beginning after 1/1/21 are family $19,210.66, individual plus one $14,730.96, single $7,043.89, projected to $19,844.61, $15,217.08 and $7,276.34 assuming 3.3% medical CPI growth; employees contribute approximately 13% on average. Dental and vision are self-funded; workers' compensation runs through the SET-SEG Self-Insurers pool.

**Subsidies and initiatives.** Financial subsidies for cooperative services total $1,551,950: Illuminate DnA $718,300, Xello career cruising software $257,000, Nepris $192,500, Atlas Rubicon $170,000, Discovery Education Streaming $156,000, PowerSchool BusinessPlus per-pupil subsidy $27,400, CDX Automotive $15,000, Meltwater $6,750, Student Achievement Media $5,000, TV Eyes $2,400, Sprout Social $1,600. Oakland Schools is providing up to $5 million for Literacy Essentials Oakland, a five-year project launched in 2019-20, and an estimated $2 million for learning-loss programs — the Oakland Youth Innovation Lab, Design Studio, tutoring, and OSTC supplemental instruction. Other flagged commitments include a $13.6 million special education center program renovation and the STEMi mobile STEM classroom. Oakland Schools received no ESSER, Governor's Emergency Education Relief or Coronavirus Relief Fund money and will not receive ESSER II; COVID expenditures are funded with tax revenues and state aid. Fee-based programs: VLAC K-8 projected at 295 FTE at $6,450 resident / $6,650 non-resident; VLAC 9-12 at 30 FTE, $6,700 / $6,900; the Accelerated College Experience at an estimated 180 students, $4,900 per pupil — none increased from 2020-21.

**Cost allocation.** Costs are spread across the three major funds using a general allocation of 50% GEF / 25% SEF / 25% CFEF, an FTE-based activity method at 24/24/52, space utilization at 50/24/26, transportation miles at 73/25/2, and a property-tax millage split of 6% / 75.5% / 18.5%. Allocated departments total $25,307,700 — Fund 100 $11,267,800, Fund 200 $6,262,000, Fund 600 $7,777,900 — or 11.19%. The Special Education Fund carries a 25% maximum allocation cap on each eligible function-based cost pool under MDE rules and Bulletin 1022.

**Other funds.** Shared Services & Tuition Programs Fund 270: revenue $16,166,200, expenditures $16,123,700, ending balance $3,157,400. Oakland Network for Education (ONE) Fund 271, a fiber network with 29 consortium members: revenue $1,297,000, expenditures $572,000, committed balance $7,725,800. Medicaid Fund 273: revenue and expenditures both $11,133,300, including $10,454,900 transferred to LEAs; Medicaid billing is expected to generate approximately $10.5 million of revenue for LEAs. HR/Finance Consortium Fund 277, formed by 22 districts as MiPEER: revenue $1,224,300, expenditures $1,396,000, balance $307,600; Oakland Schools transferred a net $4,875,000 from the CPDI Fund between FY 2012-13 and FY 2015-16. School Activities Fund 290 (created under GASB 84): $180,000 in and out, balance $298,200. Debt Service Fund 311, the 2016 Refunding Bonds with payments through 2036: revenue $1,847,000, expenditures $2,096,900, balance $4,147,300. Fund 313, the 2010 Qualified School Construction Bond running through 2027: revenue $5,500, expenditures $812,500, balance $2,038,300. Fund 314: revenue $1,572,200 including a $760,200 federal interest subsidy, expenditures $927,500, balance $11,062,000. Capital Projects Fund 404: revenue $2,308,000, expenditures $2,532,700, balance $5,450,100. Fund 406 (Administration Building): revenue $811,000, expenditures $1,639,000, balance $7,307,900. Fund 409 (Career Connections): revenue $200, expenditures $30,000, balance $500,800. Production Print Enterprise Fund 710: revenue $1,740,200, expenses $1,824,800, total net position $1,099,400. Risk Related Activity Fund 810: revenue $9,802,400, expenses $9,785,300, net position $1,841,400; compensated absence liabilities are fully funded, with a total provision of $4,010,300.

**Grants.** Total $92,051,400. Fund 105 General Education projects $34,354,600 — new awards $28,629,900 including Section 32d Great Start Readiness $20,448,600, Title I Regional Assistance $2,735,300, Section 35a4 Early Literacy Teacher Coach $2,137,500, Great Start Readiness Transportation $894,100, Wraparound Oakland County Health Network $561,000, Section 32p Early Childhood Block Grant $565,700, MiSTEM Network Region $279,900, Section 74 School Bus Driver Safety $255,300; carryover $5,724,700. Fund 205 Special Education $55,749,000 — IDEA Flowthrough $44,829,600, IDEA Preschool $1,363,700, Early-On Michigan $949,600, Section 54d Early On $653,000, IDEA General Supervision $191,400; carryover $7,707,700. Fund 605 Vocational $1,947,800 — Perkins Regional Allocation $1,694,800, Section 61b CTE Early Middle Dual Enrollment $229,300, Section 99h FIRST Robotics $23,700.

**Capital and debt.** The 5-Year Capital Outlay Plan received first reading March 16, 2021; FY21–FY26 projected needs total $34,351,500 against $15,950,000 of net transfers, leaving an estimated 6/30/2026 surplus of $3,428,300; the FY2022 need is $5,036,500. Debt service expenditures are $975,000 principal redemption and $2,045,400 interest, $3,020,400 total.

**Governance and statute.** Board policies 3050 (budget preparation), 3100 (annual operating budget and amendments), 3150 (fund balance) and 3170 (budget transfer authority) govern the process; changes flow through budget amendments at least three times each fiscal year, and inter-fund transfers require prior Board approval. The GEF and Career Focused Education Fund unassigned/restricted balance targets rise .5% each year from 5%–10% in FY 2017-18 to 7.5%–12.5% in fiscal year 2022-23. Compliance obligations cited: the General Property Tax Act, PA 206 of 1893 (MCL 211.24e); the Uniform Budgeting and Accounting Act, PA 2 of 1968; the Revised School Code, PA 451 of 1976 (MCL 380.624 and MCL 380.684); and the Michigan School Accounting Manual, Bulletin 1022. The proposed budget must go to each constituent district board by May 1 and be adopted no later than June 30. County context includes the Oakland80 goal of 80% of adults holding a post-secondary credential by 2030 and emerging-sector investment of over $5.4 billion with almost 55,000 jobs created and over 40,300 retained as of December 2020.
